angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 267,149 km at 50.22 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 19.9111 +/- 0.0129 mas (same row, RUWE 1.32): 50.22 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.384 +/- 0.018 solar radii from Jiang et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2094 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547ag367J/abstract): 267,149 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.425 +/- 0.059 solar masses from Jiang et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2094 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547ag367J/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3435 +/- 55 K from Jiang et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2094 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547ag367J/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Jiang et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2094 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547ag367J/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2094.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.898, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
